2607.27428.title: Rethinking Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging: Assumptions, Reality, and Reframing
2607.27428.paper_summary: Medical imaging has served as primary proving ground for clinical artificial intelligence (AI), yet a decade of intense research has not translated into proportionate bedside impact. We argue that this gap is not primarily a product of insufficient algorithmic performance, inadequate regulation, or limited explainability. Rather, it reflects a structural misalignment, between how AI systems are designed and evaluated, and how clinical decisions are made. This Perspective identifies six interconnected dimensions of this misalignment: the dominance of pixel-only models in a multimodal clinical world; the erosion of physician trust through opaque and inflexible systems; the unfulfilled promise of foundation models in data-sparse medical domains; the persistent bottleneck of non-shareable, under-curated datasets; the gap between validated algorithms and deployable clinical platforms; and the failure of prediction-centric AI to generate actionable clinical guidance. For each dimension, we reframe the problem and propose a path forward, culminating in a vision of agentic, physician-aligned AI that extends, rather than replaces, clinical judgment.
2607.27428.paper_summary_zh: 醫學影像一直是臨床人工智慧（AI）的主要試驗場，然而十年的密集研究並未轉化為相應的床邊影響。我們認為這一差距並非主要源於算法性能不足、監管不充分或可解釋性有限。相反，它反映出一種結構性不對齊，體現在AI系統的設計和評估方式與臨床決策的制定方式之間。這篇觀點文章確定了這種不對齊的六個相互關聯的維度：在多模態臨床世界中，僅依賴像素的模型的主導地位；通過不透明和不靈活的系統侵蝕醫生的信任；在數據稀缺的醫療領域中，基礎模型未能實現的承諾；不可共享、未經精心策劃的數據集持續存在的瓶頸；經過驗證的算法與可部署的臨床平台之間的差距；以及以預測為中心的AI未能生成可行的臨床指導。對於每個維度，我們重新框定問題並提出前進的路徑，最終形成一種代理性、與醫生對齊的AI願景，這種AI是延伸而非取代臨床判斷。
